title: Durable pinned checkpoint manifest
description: FORK-PIN-01: a durable, content-addressed copy of an execution-fork checkpoint (see clozn.checkpoint-reference.v1, whose lifecycle is deliberately ephemeral/worker-memory-only). A pinned-checkpoint manifest survives worker restart and FIFO eviction: the KV bytes live in the content-addressed blob store (blob.sha256), keyed independently of any worker's process generation. `identity` is the fail-closed compatibility fingerprint every /v1/checkpoint/import call re-checks before resolving this pin against a (possibly different) worker -- see engine/core/serve/checkpoint_codec.hpp.

Source.description: Provenance of the ephemeral in-memory checkpoint this pin was exported from. worker_generation_id is recorded for audit only -- a pin is NEVER resolved by comparing it, only `identity` below is (see checkpoint_codec.hpp's checkpoint_identity_json comment: comparing worker_generation_id at import would defeat the entire point of a durable pin).

Identity.description: The engine/model identity fingerprint every /v1/checkpoint/import call fail-closes on. Mirrors engine/core/serve/server_main.cpp's checkpoint_identity_json() exactly.

Blob.description: sha256 is the content address of the raw KV bytes ONLY (the tensor_store.py binary-blob convention: .bin blob + .json sidecar, keyed by the same digest). payload_sha256 is the engine's OWN inner hash (kv + tokens + n_past + sampler + steer, see hash_checkpoint_payload) re-verified by /v1/checkpoint/import on resolution -- a different value from sha256 by design (different inputs, different job).
